statement: The current Jurançon specification distinguishes three white-wine paths in the same geography: Jurançon sec at no more than 4 grams per litre of fermentable sugars, Jurançon above 40 grams per litre, and Jurançon vendanges tardives above 55 grams per litre.

The current Jurançon specification names Gros Manseng and Petit Manseng as principal varieties and Camaralet de Lasseube, Courbu, Lauzet and Petit Courbu as accessory varieties; the vendanges tardives mention is reserved to the two Mansengs.

All Jurançon grapes are hand harvested. Successive picking passes are required except for Jurançon sec, while vendanges tardives fruit cannot be harvested before 2 November; off-vine passerillage is prohibited apart from handling within the parcel during harvest.

Jurançon’s wet Atlantic foothills are tempered in autumn by a frequent warm, dry southerly foehn. On steep slopes and terraces, late, thick-skinned local grapes can concentrate while retaining high acidity and resisting grey rot, which helps explain how dry, sweet and late-harvest wines remain distinct paths rather than different places.

Camin Larredya publishes its estate address at Chapelle de Rousse, 1901 Chemin Larredya, in the commune of Jurançon; CARTA maps that production base, not its vineyard parcels or purchased-fruit sources.

scope_notes: The stated 9.5-hectare estate and 4 hectares of terraces are estate-vine scopes. Fruit purchased from other growers is a separate scope on the source page.
statement: Camin Larredya describes a 9.5-hectare certified-organic estate, including 4 hectares of terraces, planted mainly to Petit Manseng and Gros Manseng with Petit Courbu and Camaralet completing the estate mix.
Domaine Cauhapé describes a Monein estate on southeast-facing Jurançon slopes, with vineyards rising to about 400 metres and a range that deliberately includes both dry and sweet wines.
Clos Uroulat publishes its base in Monein’s Quartier Trouilh; the current departmental tourism record describes a six-wine visitor range spanning three dry wines, one tender wine and two sweet wines.

The Vignerons du Jurançon association places Domaine de Souch at 805 Chemin de Souch in Laroin and describes a 7-hectare estate working Petit Manseng, Gros Manseng and Courbu with organic farming, biodynamic principles and manual harvests.
